claims.text: The starting CoCrFeNiTi alloy is an equimolar or near-equimolar, homogeneous, single-phase disordered solid solution.
As-processed equimolar CoCrFeNiTi has relatively low hardness and strength.
As-processed equimolar CoCrFeNiTi has favorable plasticity and machinability.
The low hardness and strength result from the alloy's simple solid-solution state and its lack of nanoscale dislocation obstacles.
The disordered solid solution has weak lattice friction.
Weak lattice friction permits nearly unimpeded dislocation glide.
Nearly unimpeded dislocation glide produces high plasticity but low strength and hardness.
A heat treatment can induce nanoscale precipitates or short-range ordered clusters in CoCrFeNiTi.
The proposed nanoscale ordering can be induced without altering the alloy's overall phase structure.
Nanoscale precipitates or short-range ordered clusters impede and pin dislocations.
Dislocation pinning by the induced nanoscale obstacles increases yield strength and hardness.
Dislocation pinning by the induced nanoscale obstacles reduces ductility.
The heat-treated alloy should exhibit a statistically significant increase in hardness relative to the as-processed alloy.
The heat-treated alloy should exhibit a statistically significant increase in yield strength relative to the as-processed alloy.
The heat-treated alloy should exhibit a modest reduction in ductility relative to the as-processed alloy.
Nanoscale precipitates or ordered clusters should be present after heat treatment and absent from the baseline alloy.
The hypothesis is asserted to apply from approximately 25 °C to 600 °C.
The hypothesis is limited to moderate mechanical loading regimes in which catastrophic failure is avoided.

contradictions.description: The intervention is required not to alter the overall phase structure, yet one proposed and predicted mediator is the formation of nanoscale precipitates, which ordinarily constitutes phase separation. Short-range ordering could satisfy the constraint, but the precipitate branch is in tension with it.
